candidates.change_summary: Removed the require guard so anyone can call withdraw() and withdraw contract balance to Owner.
Changed the transfer recipient from Owner to msg.sender, so caller receives the contract balance after withdraw().
Added a guard that requires msg.sender to NOT be Owner, inverting the original check so non-owners can trigger transfer to Owner.
Made withdraw() transfer zero instead of the contract balance, so no funds are moved.
Added an extra transfer of the contract balance to Owner before the original transfer, causing double transfer attempts.

Replace external call adr.call{value: msg.value}(data) with a low-level staticcall (disallowing value transfer) which will change behavior when Command attempts to send Ether or modify state on target.
Replace adr.call{value: msg.value}(data) with a call that forwards zero value (adr.call(data)), altering behavior when msg.value is expected to be forwarded.
Replace adr.call{value: msg.value}(data) with a direct low-level call that forwards all contract balance instead of msg.value, changing transferred value semantics.
Insert a require that msg.value must be zero before making the call, preventing forwarding of any Ether and reverting when value sent, changing observable behavior when sender provides value.
Replace adr.call{value: msg.value}(data) with a call that checks and reverts on failure (require(success)), changing behavior when the callee fails (previously ignored).
Change transfer target from payable(adr) to payable(msg.sender) so the contract sends its balance+msg.value to the caller instead of the provided address.

Invert the if condition to require msg.value < address(this).balance, making the transfer happen only when the sent value is smaller than the contract balance and thus changing when and whether funds are moved.
Remove the require guard that checks for overflow on (address(this).balance + msg.value), allowing transfer to proceed without that check.
